comparison.text: Official Indian AQI: 64 out of 500, category 'Satisfactory'. That is the government's own scale.
comparison.source_name: CPCB, National Air Quality Index (PM2.5 breakpoints)
comparison.caveat: Computed from PM2.5 alone. The full CPCB AQI takes the worst sub-index across pollutants, so the official city AQI can be higher on days another pollutant dominates.

comparison.text: A week of air like this = 5.5 cigarettes. Your lungs are keeping the receipts.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence
comparison.caveat: Extends the Berkeley Earth per-day rule of thumb across a week at the same level. Real weeks vary day to day.

comparison.text: That is 1.8x the WHO daily safe limit. The limit is 15. We are not close.
comparison.source_name: WHO, 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines (PM2.5 24-hour average 15 ug/m3)
comparison.caveat: WHO guidelines are health-based targets, not legal limits. India's own national standard (60 ug/m3 for 24h PM2.5) is four times looser.

comparison.text: Today's air is worse than 98 percent of days this season in Bengaluru. Ranked, logged, versioned.
comparison.caveat: Season means the trailing 90 days of this project's own observations. Small archive early on means noisy percentiles, and the repo shows exactly how small.
